facts.claim: The official vLLM playbook uses the NGC image nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:${LATEST_VLLM_VERSION} with example tag 26.05.post1-py3, plus upstream images vllm/vllm-openai:gemma, vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-cu130 and vllm/vllm-openai:latest; multi-node uses Ray via run_cluster.sh pinned to vllm commit 51c1ee9b7c8acbba4899a8ebffd390685d171946.
facts.detail: Multi-node env vars passed to the container: VLLM_HOST_IP, UCX_NET_DEVICES=$MN_IF_NAME, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$MN_IF_NAME, OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=$MN_IF_NAME, GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$MN_IF_NAME, TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$MN_IF_NAME, RAY_memory_monitor_refresh_ms=0, MASTER_ADDR. Example MN_IF_NAME is enp1s0f1np1. Ray dashboard at http://<head-node-ip>:8265. Prereq check: nvcc --version confirms CUDA 13.0. The playbook's VLLM_IMAGE example is written as 'nccr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3' (apparent typo for nvcr.io). Health check: 'timeout 900 bash -c until curl -sf http://localhost:8000/health'. Troubleshooting: 'CUDA out of memory' -> reduce --max-model-len/--max-num-seqs; 'Container startup fails' -> verify ARM64 image; memory pressure -> sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'.

facts.claim: Playbook issue #109 (2026-08-24) reports the nvidia/vllm multi-node tutorial is now broken because current vLLM (including NVIDIA's NGC image) no longer ships Ray as a dependency.
facts.detail: Title: 'nvidia/vllm is wrong missing Ray'. Reporter built a custom image adding Ray. References vllm-project/vllm#33445. The playbook's sed line already tries to 'pip install -q --root-user-action=ignore ray[default]>=2.9' before 'ray start'.

facts.claim: Ollama playbook: install with 'curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh'; API port 11434; binary /usr/local/bin/ollama; data dir /usr/share/ollama; service user 'ollama'; uninstall via systemctl stop/disable ollama, rm /usr/local/bin/ollama, rm -rf /usr/share/ollama, userdel ollama.
facts.detail: Gotchas quoted: 'Connection refused' means 'SSH tunnel not active'; 'Ollama command not found' requires terminal restart; slow inference suggests model exceeds GPU memory capacity. Check with 'ollama --version', 'ollama list', 'curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags'.

facts.claim: llama.cpp playbook builds natively with cmake -B build -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CURL=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real; the performance benchmarking guide instead uses -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="121a" -DGGML_CUDA_CUB_3DOT2=on.
facts.detail: Build deps: sudo apt install -y git clang cmake libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev. Troubleshooting: 'CUDA not found' during CMake -> export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH; wrong GPU architecture error -> -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="121"; connection refused on port 30000 -> check 'server is listening' and ss -tln; CUDA OOM -> lower --ctx-size or smaller quant; high latency -> increase --n-gpu-layers and check nvidia-smi utilization. Server default in playbook: --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000. llama-bench flags: -ngl 99 -dio 1 -fa 1.

facts.claim: SGLang playbook uses image lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130, launches with python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --attention-backend flashinfer --mem-fraction-static 0.75, and requires --quantization modelopt_fp4 for NVFP4 models.
facts.detail: Verification: docker run --rm --gpus all "$SGLANG_IMAGE" nvidia-smi. UMA memory issue fix quoted: sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. Allow 60 s for server init before assuming failure. Port 30000.

facts.claim: TensorRT-LLM playbook uses nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc13 (single node) and nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc5 (multi-node), serves on port 8355 (LLM) / 8356 (VLM), passes --device /dev/infiniband:/dev/infiniband and UCX_NET_DEVICES / NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME = enp1s0f0np0,enp1s0f1np1 for two nodes.
facts.detail: Troubleshooting table quoted: 'OOM during weight loading' -> export TRT_LLM_DISABLE_LOAD_WEIGHTS_IN_PARALLEL=1; host OOM on first run -> drop_caches; 'ptxas fatal' compilation errors -> add -x TRITON_PTXAS_PATH to mpirun; 'invalid mount config for type bind' -> check trtllm-mn-entrypoint.sh; system clock out of sync -> sudo timedatectl set-ntp true; port 2233 in use -> entrypoint won't start; UCX network warnings safe to ignore when one CX-7 port unused; container exit 255 -> docker logs. Serving uses PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True and OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1. Config yaml keys: kv_cache_config.free_gpu_memory_fraction 0.80/0.9, moe_config.backend CUTLASS, cuda_graph_config.enable_padding true, disable_overlap_scheduler true. Prereqs oddly say 'CUDA 12.x drivers'.

facts.claim: NCCL playbook builds NCCL v2.30.7-1 with make -j src.build NVCC_GENCODE="-gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121", uses management interface enP7s7 (or Wi-Fi wlP9s9) for UCX_NET_DEVICES / NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME / OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include, and for ring (3+ node) topologies sets NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1 and NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none.
facts.detail: Paths: CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda, MPI_HOME=/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/openmpi, NCCL_HOME=$HOME/nccl/build/. Check ports with ibdev2netdev and ip addr show enP7s7. All nodes must use the same interface type. When two QSFP cables are connected, all four interfaces must have IPs. mpirun hosts need ':1' suffix.

facts.claim: Playbook issue #102 (2026-08-17) shows the NCCL playbook defaults plateau at ~3 GB/s busbw; reaching ~190 Gbps (23.74 GB/s) required NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0, MTU 9000 on the CX-7 interfaces (default is 1500), and rebuilding NCCL from release tag v2.28.9-1; the recommended 16G all_gather_perf test allocates ~32 GB/node and froze the system (hard power cycle) when a desktop session was active.
facts.detail: Environment: 2x DGX Spark, single QSFP 200G DAC, DGX OS 7.5.0, kernel 6.17.0-1029-nvidia. Raw RDMA per port half: 109 Gbps. Proposed safer sweep: -b 512M -e 4G -f 2.

facts.claim: connect-two-sparks: each CX-7 physical QSFP port exposes two logical interfaces (enp1s0f0np0 + enP2p1s0f0np0, enp1s0f1np1 + enP2p1s0f1np1); persistent config lives in /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml (chmod 600, netplan apply) with example subnets 192.168.100.x/24 and 192.168.101.x/24; ip-addr-add config is lost on reboot.
facts.detail: discover-sparks helper script: refuses to run as root ('Error: This script should not be run as root or with sudo'), parses ibdev2netdev for interfaces marked 'Up)', requires avahi-browse ('Error: avahi-browse not found. Please install avahi-utils package.'), browses _ssh._tcp, generates ed25519 keys, prints 'Shared SSH setup complete!'. Gotcha: 'Use the same physical port on each device to prevent issues'.

facts.claim: The performance_benchmarking_guide.md tests RDMA with ib_write_bw -d rocep1s0f0 -i 1 -p 12000 -F --report_gbits (single link example 92.57 Gb/sec) and ib_write_lat -p 13000; fine-tuning requires export BNB_CUDA_VERSION=130 ('Force bitsandbytes to use CUDA 13.0 binary (CUDA 13.1 not yet supported)'); netplan for RDMA uses renderer NetworkManager and may need re-applying after reboot.
facts.detail: Serving defaults in guide: trtllm-serve --backend pytorch; vllm serve --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9; sglang --mem-fraction-static 0.75; llama-server -fa 1. Guide states 'DGX Spark uses a long-term supported (LTS) base software stack' and to prefer NGC containers over direct CUDA installs.

facts.claim: PyTorch fine-tune playbook uses nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.11-py3 (also 25.10-py3), and for two-node training uses Docker Swarm with /etc/docker/daemon.json 'default-runtime': 'nvidia' plus 'node-generic-resources': ['NVIDIA_GPU=GPU-<uuid>'] and uncomments swarm-resource in /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml.
facts.detail: GPU UUID from 'nvidia-smi -a | grep UUID'. Debug env vars: ACCELERATE_DEBUG_MODE=1, ACCELERATE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, TORCH_CPP_LOG_LEVEL=INFO, TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL. Docker recovery: systemctl stop docker; rm -rf /var/lib/docker/swarm; systemctl start docker. Scripts: Llama3_3B_full_finetuning.py, Llama3_8B_LoRA_finetuning.py, Llama3_70B_LoRA_finetuning.py, Llama3_70B_qLoRA_finetuning.py.

facts.claim: ComfyUI playbook installs torch via 'pip3 install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130', clones ComfyUI --branch v0.28.2, and serves on port 8188 with --listen 0.0.0.0; setup.sh/launch.sh SHA256 are 97b03fb3... and 7dc75b15....
facts.detail: Troubleshooting: 'PyTorch CUDA not available' -> verify torch.cuda.is_available(); web UI inaccessible -> open port 8188; UMA memory issues -> drop_caches.

facts.claim: DGX Dashboard runs on port 11000 (http://localhost:11000); per-user JupyterLab ports are stored in /opt/nvidia/dgx-dashboard-service/jupyterlab_ports.yaml; system updates from the dashboard upgrade packages and firmware and trigger a reboot.
facts.detail: Remote access: ssh -L 11000:localhost:11000 -L <ASSIGNED_PORT>:localhost:<ASSIGNED_PORT> user@spark. Default JupyterLab dir /home/<USERNAME>/jupyterlab. NVIDIA staff on the forum point to https://localhost:11000 as the sanctioned memory view since nvidia-smi cannot report it.

facts.claim: natolambert/dgx-spark-setup documents the core GB10 ML gotcha: the ecosystem ships CUDA 12.x wheels, producing 'ImportError: libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file'; fix is torch from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 and vLLM from https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu130, and never installing flash-attn on aarch64.
facts.detail: Reported specs: 119.68 GB unified memory visible, 20 ARM cores, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.95.05, Ubuntu 24.04. Env: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1a", TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas, VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MXFP4_MOE=1, PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64. Errors: "sm_121a is not defined for option 'gpu-name'" -> TRITON_PTXAS_PATH; 'FlashAttention2 has been toggled on, but flash_attn is not installed' -> attn_implementation=sdpa; vLLM load hang -> --vllm_enforce_eager. Safe-to-ignore PyTorch warning: 'Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1. Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)'. Memory advice: disable swap (sudo swapoff -a; edit /etc/fstab) because 'GPU OOM = System OOM' and swap makes the machine go 'zombie'; run jobs in systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=100G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMScoreAdjust=500; protect sshd via /etc/systemd/system/ssh.service.d/oom.conf with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 MemoryMin=512M; watchdog kills job when MemAvailable < 16 GB. Memory scales super-linearly with batch size (8->16 added 34 GB).

facts.claim: Sggin1/DGX-SPARK records baselines: March 2026 driver 580.142 with CUDA 13.0/13.2 toolkits; June 2026 driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0.2, DGX OS 7.5.0. It notes ptxas refuses tcgen05.mma for sm_121a, pip install mamba-ssm is broken on aarch64, and that '/proc/meminfo beats nvidia-smi' for detecting real memory pressure.
facts.detail: nvfp4 notes: default gpu_memory_utilization~0.9 over-allocates KV cache on 128 GB UMA; torch.compile + CUDA graphs can consume tens of GB; FlashInfer JIT first use triggers multi-GB cicc spikes; old env vars VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND=marlin / VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=0 are deprecated in favor of --linear-backend / --moe-backend; native SM120/121 CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM landed in vLLM PR #40082 (May 2026). Other folders: turboquant (vLLM PR #38479), fp4_SASS ('1 PFLOP FP4 pipe is a silicon gap on GB10'), dual-spark, flightrec, recipes.

facts.claim: Sggin1 GX10_PD_Throttle_Fix.md: a USB-C PD controller firmware wedge in the 240 W brick leaves the GPU 'pinned at 611 MHz / ~13 W / thermal cap at ~50 C under load'; only a full cold drain (shutdown, unplug PSU and all USB-C, hold power 30 s, wait 60 s) resets it; healthy is '~2200 MHz / ~93 W / ~56 bf16 TFLOPS'.
facts.detail: Post-recovery firmware flash: sudo fwupdmgr refresh; sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades; sudo fwupdmgr update --assume-yes --no-reboot-check; a second cold drain is required for new firmware to load; fwupdmgr get-devices 'Current version' may still show the old value (trust 'Update State: Success' and a load test with clock >=1400 MHz, power >=40 W). ASUS GX10 target firmware 0x00000507 (LVFS release 133405). Triggers: sleep/resume, mid-load crashes, warm reboots after firmware updates.

facts.claim: Sggin1 comfyui_spark_notes: PyPI 'onnxruntime' (CPU-only 1.26.0) silently overwrites the community 'onnxruntime-gpu' 1.25.0 sm_121 wheel because both install to site-packages/onnxruntime/; detection is ort.get_available_providers() returning ['AzureExecutionProvider', 'CPUExecutionProvider'] instead of ['CUDAExecutionProvider', 'CPUExecutionProvider'].
facts.detail: Symptom: DWPose/controlnet preprocessors silently fall back to CPU. Prevention: pin onnxruntime-gpu==1.25.0 in requirements.txt.

facts.claim: Sggin1 DUAL_SPARK_SETUP.md: dual-Spark NCCL over a single CX-7 cable needs NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none, NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1, NCCL_IB_MERGE_NICS=0, NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3 (RoCE v2); 'ibv_modify_qp failed 101' means wrong GID index; the two twin interfaces must be on separate subnets or NCCL errors 'Interfaces X and Y share the same subnet'; UFW blocks Ray GCS ('GCS health check failed: 10.10.0.1:29501').
facts.detail: Uses nmcli with 802-3-ethernet.mtu 9000; validate with ping -c 2 -M do -s 8000. Expected: ~107 Gb/s per twin, 195-197 Gb/s aggregate, GPU stress 80-140 TFLOP/s sustained. Notable: 'ignore dmesg | grep insufficient power - on Spark those mlx5 PCIe warnings fire at boot even on healthy power'. Verify NCCL used IB: docker logs ... | grep -E 'NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX|NET/IB' should show 'Initialized NET plugin IB' not 'NET/Socket'.

facts.claim: tonyd2wild/dgx-spark-hard-poweroff-fix: log-less hard power-offs under sustained GPU load (no shutdown record in 'last -Fx', journal ends abruptly, no OOM/panic/Xid/thermal, /sys/fs/pstore empty, kdump inactive, kernel taint 4096) were eliminated by capping GPU clocks with 'sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200' (~5% throughput cost), persisted via a gb10-clock-cap.service systemd unit.
facts.detail: Verify: nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK | head -20; revert: sudo nvidia-smi -rgc. Clock lock persists only while the driver stays loaded; DGX Spark runs nvidia-persistenced by default. Firmware split: production 'GX10DGX.0104' (Mar-2026) vs pre-production '5.36_0ACUM018'. RMA path: fielddiag reports thermal error '082-000-1-020000600139'. 'free -g misrepresents CUDA-allocatable memory on GB10'. Results: '~20 log-less hard-offs in 3 weeks' -> zero after cap; 30.8 vs 32.3 tok/s.

facts.claim: martimramos/dgx-spark-ml-guide (older, cu128-nightly era) documents that PyTorch nightly's bundled libnvrtc.so.12 'does not recognize sm_121 as a valid --gpu-architecture value' and fixes it by symlinking /usr/local/cuda-13.0/lib64/libnvrtc.so.13 over site-packages/nvidia/cuda_nvrtc/lib/libnvrtc.so.12; it also states NGC PyTorch <=24.10 lacked sm_121 while NGC >=25.10 supports GB10.
facts.detail: Env for source builds: FORCE_CUDA=1 TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.0" FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS="120" FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE MAX_JOBS=4 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda. docker-compose must use deploy.resources.reservations.devices (driver: nvidia, count: all, capabilities: [gpu, compute, utility]) rather than 'runtime: nvidia'. onnx==1.16.0 is the only aarch64 wheel; DataLoader num_workers=0 advised. Expected torch check: 'CUDA: True | Device: NVIDIA GB10'.

facts.claim: ogulcanaydogan/dgx-spark-llm-stack pins PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130, Triton 3.5.1, Python 3.12, GCC 13.3 for GB10 and sets VLLM_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS=0 ('Disable custom C++ ops on DGX Spark'), TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas, VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN; it notes 'Official wheels max out at sm_120, emit warnings on sm_121', flash-attention lacks sm_121 kernels (use SDPA), and TransformerEngine MXFP8 training is unsupported.
facts.detail: HW_PROFILE=dgx-spark|h100. Build times: PyTorch ~4 h, all ~6 h. Verification: python scripts/verify_install.py; scripts/check_compatibility.py.

facts.claim: k8s-device-plugin issue #1482 (2025-10-29): on GB10 with driver 580.95.05 / CUDA 13.0, nvidia-smi shows memory 'Not Supported' and the plugin crashed with 'error getting device memory: Not Supported'; a maintainer closed it 2026-05-14 ('Closing for GB10 as the fix is alreday there'); v0.17.4 changelog contains 'Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML'.
facts.detail: Full error: 'error starting plugins: error getting plugins: unable to create plugins: failed to construct resource managers: error building device map: error building device map from config.resources: error building GPU device map: error visiting device: error building Device: error getting device memory: Not Supported'. A 2026-01-02 comment shows 'nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-9kt9b 0/1 CrashLoopBackOff' with 390 restarts; a 2026-03-31 comment (driver 580.126.09) says MPS fails ('getpwuid() failed for 0') and only time-slicing works. gpu-operator #1794 (v25.3.4, DGXOS 7, k3s) hit the same error. dra-driver-nvidia-gpu #1073 (2026-04-23, DRA v25.12.0, GPU Operator v26.3.1, driver 595.58.03) hit 'error getting memory info for device 0: Not Supported' and was fixed by PR #1121. Note: the fetched v0.17.4 release page showed a 2024 date, which conflicts with its CUDA 13.0.0 base image bump; treat the date as unverified.

facts.claim: The community NVML replacement is CINOAdam/nvml-unified-shim (forum thread 358869, posted 2026-01-28): an LD_PRELOAD/drop-in libnvidia-ml.so.1 that answers nvmlDeviceGetCount, nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex, nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo (from /proc/meminfo + CUDA runtime usage) and nvmlDeviceGetName via the CUDA runtime.
facts.detail: Problem strings from the thread: MAX Engine 'No supported "gpu" device available'; 'pynvml library returns NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED'; 'nvidia-smi shows: Driver/library version mismatch'; shim's own failure message 'CUDA information: NVML: Unable to get memory info'. Build: make; sudo make install -> /usr/local/lib/libnvml-unified.so (thread also shows make -f Makefile.python). Usage: LD_PRELOAD=./libnvml-unified.so nvtop; debug with NVML_SHIM_DEBUG=1. Limitations: fake index-as-pointer handles, GPU utilization reports 0%, still reports PCIe metrics, no fan/thermal. NVIDIA staff reply (aniculescu) only moved it to GB10 projects.

facts.claim: The DGX Spark Memory Dashboard is hectorTSH/dgx-spark-memory-dashboard (v0.1.0, 2026-08-26): zero-dependency Python, port 7474, derives free memory from MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo ('correct on GB10 UMA'), model residency from Ollama /api/ps, vLLM docker stats and /metrics, llama.cpp/SGLang /v1/models; motivated by nvidia-smi memory fields showing [N/A] on GB10.
facts.detail: Run: python3 scripts/run.py --demo | -c config.yaml [--host 0.0.0.0]; pip install -e . then dgx-spark-memory-dashboard --demo. README: 'Classic nvidia-smi VRAM bars lie or return [N/A]'.

facts.claim: NVIDIA's DGX Spark Known Issues page states nvidia-smi reports 'Memory-Usage: Not Supported' on the iGPU as expected behaviour (no dedicated framebuffer) while per-process GPU memory is still listed, and that cudaMemGetInfo reports less allocatable memory than actually available because of DRAM reclamation; the documented mitigation is sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. It also warns to use only the supplied power adapter or risk reduced performance, boot failure, or unexpected shutdowns.
facts.detail: Forum staff confirmation (thread 367765, April 2026): 'The DGX Spark has a unified memory architecture. NVIDIA-SMI only reports memory utilization when there is dedicated GPU VRAM.' Suggested tools: top, htop, free, DGX Dashboard https://localhost:11000.

facts.claim: Driver 580.159.03 (announced 2026-06-11) adds 'enhancements to Out-of-Memory (OOM) handling with GB10's unified memory architecture' and 'user feedback when the system encounters memory pressure'; it is delivered via the 'Update' button in the DGX Spark Dashboard.
facts.detail: OTA2607 (2026-07-15) pairs with nvidia-driver-580-open 580.159.03-0ubuntu0.24.04.1.

facts.claim: Forum thread 378200 (2026-07-26): an apt upgrade that pulled nvidia-driver-580-open 580.173.02-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 from Ubuntu noble-updates/restricted onto a system on OTA2607 (paired with 580.159.03) broke the GPU: nvidia-smi 'No devices were found', dmesg 'NVRM: Xid (PCI:000f:01:00): 119, Timeout after 6s of waiting for RPC response from GPU0 GSP!', 'NVRM: ksec2PrepareBootCommands_GB20B: SEC2 secure boot partition timed out.', 'NVRM: RmInitAdapter: Cannot initialize GSP firmware RM', 'RmInitAdapter failed! (0x62:0x65:2028)'.
facts.detail: 'nvidia-spark-ota-check summary' reported failed: ["driver"] with 152/153 checks passing. Kernel module packages: linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-6.17.0-1026-nvidia. Resolution: updating via the DGX Dashboard re-paired driver and firmware. Later sources (playbook issues #97/#107, Sept 2026 thermal thread) show 580.173.02 running fine on DGX OS 7.5.0 / kernel 6.17.0-1029/1031-nvidia, implying a later OTA paired it.

facts.claim: Forum thread 367655 (April 2026): after a restore, a user installed nvidia-driver-580-open, nvidia-dkms-580-open-server, nvidia-fabricmanager-580, nvidia-system-station and nvidia-nvswitch-580 and got 'NVIDIA-GB10 not supported'; NVIDIA staff said 'DGX Spark does not have an NVSwitch, so Nvidia Fabric Manager is not needed' and to use only the driver provided with the OS image (System Recovery fixed it).
facts.detail: Staff referenced the DGX Spark FAQ item #7 on nvidia-smi reporting behaviour and the System Recovery Guide.

facts.claim: Forum thread 350646 (Nov-Dec 2025): 'docker: Error response from daemon: unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia' on a fresh Spark was fixed by 'nvidia-ctk runtime configure' + 'service docker restart', which writes runtimes.nvidia (path nvidia-container-runtime) into /etc/docker/daemon.json; installed toolkit was nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.0-1 arm64; a moderator noted '--gpus=all' alone suffices on DGX Spark.
facts.detail: Playbooks consistently use 'docker run --gpus all' and fix 'Permission denied' with sudo usermod -aG docker $USER; newgrp docker.

facts.claim: Playbook issues #97 (2026-08-12) and #116 (2026-08-31) describe GB10 hard resets / loss of host reachability under memory pressure with no OOM-killer, Xid, thermal or panic logs; both show preceding kernel lines 'NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] (0x00000051) returned from _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc) @ mem_desc.c:1359' and (#116) 'NVRM: _iovaspaceCreateMappingDataFromMemDesc: failed to allocate 0x176028 bytes for IOVA mapping metadata'.
facts.detail: #97: DGX OS 7.5.0, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.17.0-1029-nvidia, driver 580.173.02, container ghcr.io/anemll/dspark-vllm-gx10:0.1.1, vLLM 0.25.2.dev0, 2-node TP=2; head had ~111 GiB used / 10 GiB available / 3.8 GiB swap before a 131K-token prefill; pstore empty; 'crashkernel configured for zero bytes'. #116: kernel 6.17.0-1014-nvidia, driver 580.142, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.10.0; ~43-45 GiB MemAvailable at loss; per-sample torch.cuda.empty_cache() raised completion from 117/512 to 512/512.

detection_heuristics.what: Identify a GB10 / DGX Spark host
detection_heuristics.how: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name --format=csv,noheader == 'NVIDIA GB10'; uname -m == aarch64; kernel release contains '-nvidia' (e.g. 6.17.0-1029-nvidia); /etc/os-release Ubuntu 24.04; compute capability 12.1 via deviceQuery or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (12,1); /proc/meminfo MemTotal ~ 121-128 GiB; dpkg -l shows nvidia-driver-580-open; PCI address of GPU seen in NVRM logs is 000f:01:00.0.
exact_strings: Total amount of global memory:                 124618 MBytes

detection_heuristics.what: nvidia-smi memory fields are expected to be unavailable on GB10 (not a fault)
detection_heuristics.how: Match the Memory-Usage column / --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total output for 'Not Supported' or '[N/A]' and suppress any 'VRAM unknown' error; report unified memory from /proc/meminfo (MemTotal, MemAvailable) and /proc/pressure/memory instead. Per-process GPU memory rows are still listed.

detection_heuristics.what: NVML consumers failing on GB10 (device plugin, DRA driver, pynvml, accelerate, MAX Engine)
detection_heuristics.how: grep container/pod logs and Python tracebacks for the NVML Not Supported family; if found on a GB10 host, classify as 'NVML unified-memory limitation' and point to fixed versions or the LD_PRELOAD shim.
exact_strings: error getting device memory: Not Supported
error getting memory info for device 0: Not Supported
CUDA information: NVML: Unable to get memory info
Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!

detection_heuristics.what: Driver / GSP firmware pairing broken by an out-of-band driver upgrade
detection_heuristics.how: nvidia-smi prints 'No devices were found'; journalctl -k / dmesg contains Xid 119 GSP RPC timeout and SEC2 secure-boot messages; dpkg -l nvidia-driver-580-open version differs from the OTA-paired version (e.g. 580.173.02 on OTA2607 which pairs 580.159.03); apt policy shows the package came from noble-updates/restricted rather than the NVIDIA/DGX repo; if available, run 'nvidia-spark-ota-check summary' and look for failed: ["driver"].
exact_strings: NVRM: Xid (PCI:000f:01:00): 119, Timeout after 6s of waiting for RPC response from GPU0 GSP!
NVRM: ksec2PrepareBootCommands_GB20B: SEC2 secure boot partition timed out.
NVRM: RmInitAdapter: Cannot initialize GSP firmware RM

detection_heuristics.what: Inappropriate datacenter packages installed on Spark
detection_heuristics.how: dpkg -l | grep -E 'nvidia-fabricmanager|nvidia-nvswitch|nvidia-dkms-580-open-server|nvidia-system-station'; any hit on a GB10 host is a misconfiguration (no NVSwitch). Also flag proprietary (non -open) 580 driver packages since GB10 requires the open kernel modules shipped with the OS image.

detection_heuristics.what: NVIDIA RM out-of-memory precursors to a hard reset (unified memory exhaustion)

Suggest clock cap or power/thermal investigation.

detection_heuristics.how: Under a short cuBLAS/matmul load, sample nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.sm,power.draw,temperature.gpu,pstate,clocks_event_reasons.active --format=csv; if clocks stay < 1400 MHz and power < 20 W while pstate is P0, flag PD wedge; healthy is ~2200-2483 MHz and 80-93 W.

Likely cause: bad USB PD power negotiation

detection_heuristics.how: nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK shows locked SM clocks (e.g. max 2200 MHz vs default 2418/2483); systemctl is-enabled gb10-clock-cap.service; nvidia-smi -q shows Persistence Mode Enabled (nvidia-persistenced default on DGX OS).

detection_heuristics.how: Read /proc/meminfo MemAvailable (< 16 GiB is the community watchdog threshold) and /proc/pressure/memory 'some'/'full' avg10; note cudaMemGetInfo under-reports and free -g misrepresents CUDA-allocatable memory; suggest drop_caches as documented by NVIDIA.

candidate_rules.trigger: Host is GB10 and nvidia-smi memory fields show 'Not Supported' or '[N/A]'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: nvidia-smi reports Memory-Usage '{value}' on NVIDIA GB10; this is expected on unified-memory iGPU. Unified memory: MemTotal={memtotal}, MemAvailable={memavail} (/proc/meminfo).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Generic GPU checks would falsely report broken VRAM telemetry; NVIDIA documents this as expected behaviour, and memory must be assessed from /proc/meminfo instead.
next_steps: Use /proc/meminfo MemAvailable and /proc/pressure/memory for capacity checks
Use DGX Dashboard http://localhost:11000 or community tools (sparkview, nv-monitor, dgx-spark-memory-dashboard) for live views
Do not install NVML shims unless a specific application requires nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo

candidate_rules.trigger: Logs or tracebacks contain 'error getting device memory: Not Supported', 'NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED', 'NVMLError_NotSupported', or accelerate's 'found at least two devices, cuda:0 and cpu!' on a GB10 host
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {component} failed with '{error_string}': NVML nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo is unsupported on GB10 unified memory.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Kubernetes device plugins (< v0.17.4), DRA drivers, HAMi, accelerate device_map=auto and MAX Engine break or silently offload to CPU on GB10.
next_steps: Upgrade k8s-device-plugin to >= v0.17.4 ('Ignore errors getting device memory using NVML') / GPU Operator bundling it; DRA driver with PR #1121
For accelerate/TRT-LLM quantize.py use device_map="cuda:0" explicitly
For NVML-dependent tools consider LD_PRELOAD of CINOAdam/nvml-unified-shim (PoC; utilization reads 0%)

candidate_rules.trigger: nvidia-smi 'No devices were found' AND dmesg contains 'Xid ... 119' GSP RPC timeout or 'SEC2 secure boot partition timed out' or 'RmInitAdapter failed! (0x62:0x65:2028)'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: GPU failed GSP init: '{dmesg_line}'. Installed nvidia-driver-580-open={installed_version} (from {apt_origin}); OTA-paired driver expected {ota_version}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: On DGX OS the driver is paired with GSP/SEC2 firmware via OTA; pulling a newer driver from Ubuntu noble-updates/restricted (e.g. 580.173.02 on OTA2607) leaves the GPU unusable.
next_steps: Run 'nvidia-spark-ota-check summary' and look for failed: ["driver"]
Update through DGX Dashboard 'Update' (or documented OTA procedure) so driver and firmware are re-paired
Consider apt-mark hold on nvidia-driver-580-open to prevent unpaired upgrades
Do not disable Secure Boot as a workaround

candidate_rules.trigger: dpkg shows nvidia-fabricmanager-*, nvidia-nvswitch-*, nvidia-dkms-580-open-server or nvidia-system-station on a GB10 host, or nvidia-smi says 'NVIDIA-GB10 not supported'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Found packages {pkgs} on DGX Spark; GB10 has no NVSwitch and requires the OS-image driver.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: NVIDIA staff: 'DGX Spark does not have an NVSwitch, so Nvidia Fabric Manager is not needed'; mismatched driver stacks produced 'NVIDIA-GB10 not supported' and required System Recovery.
next_steps: Remove fabricmanager/nvswitch packages
Reinstall the driver provided with the DGX OS image (or run System Recovery)

candidate_rules.trigger: docker info lacks nvidia runtime or 'docker run --gpus all ... nvidia-smi' fails with 'unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Docker daemon at {daemon_json} has no 'nvidia' runtime; nvidia-container-toolkit {version} installed.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: All DGX Spark playbooks depend on 'docker run --gpus all'; a preinstalled but unconfigured toolkit blocks every containerized workflow.
next_steps: sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker
Add user to docker group: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER; newgrp docker
Verify: docker run --rm --gpus all <cuda-image> nvidia-smi

candidate_rules.trigger: torch.version.cuda starts with '12.' or 'ImportError: libcudart.so.12' seen while host CUDA is 13.x on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: PyTorch {torch_version} (CUDA {torch_cuda}) on CUDA {host_cuda} host; arch list {arch_list} lacks sm_121.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: CUDA 12 wheels fail to load or lack sm_121/sm_120 kernels; this is the single most common GB10 setup failure.
next_steps: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
Use NGC nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:>=25.10-py3 containers
Uninstall flash-attn / vllm-flash-attn on aarch64 and use attn_implementation="sdpa"
The warning 'cuda capability 12.1 ... supported ... (8.0) - (12.0)' is safe to ignore

candidate_rules.trigger: Logs contain "sm_121a is not defined for option 'gpu-name'" or 'ptxas fatal', or Triton is installed and TRITON_PTXAS_PATH is unset
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Triton/ptxas error '{error}'; TRITON_PTXAS_PATH={value}; system ptxas {ptxas_version}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Wheel-bundled ptxas predates sm_121a; Triton kernels (vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM) fail to compile unless the CUDA 13 ptxas is used.
next_steps: export TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas (and pass -x TRITON_PTXAS_PATH through mpirun for multi-node TRT-LLM)
Ensure /usr/local/cuda -> cuda-13.0 and /usr/local/cuda/bin on PATH

candidate_rules.trigger: Both 'onnxruntime' and 'onnxruntime-gpu' distributions installed, or get_available_providers() lacks CUDAExecutionProvider
candidate_rules.evidence_template: onnxruntime providers = {providers}; distributions: onnxruntime={v1}, onnxruntime-gpu={v2}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: The PyPI CPU wheel silently overwrites the sm_121 GPU wheel; ONNX-backed nodes fall back to CPU with no error.
next_steps: pip uninstall onnxruntime; reinstall the sm_121 onnxruntime-gpu wheel (pin onnxruntime-gpu==1.25.0)
Re-run the kit's build/onnxruntime.sh

candidate_rules.trigger: dmesg/journal contains 'NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY]' or '_iovaspaceCreateMappingDataFromMemDesc: failed to allocate'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {count} NVRM NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY events since boot (last {ts}); MemAvailable now {memavail}, swap used {swap}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: On GB10 these RM allocation failures preceded log-less hard resets and loss of network reachability (playbook issues #97, #116) with no OOM-killer or Xid trail.
next_steps: Lower --gpu-memory-utilization (0.75-0.85) / free_gpu_memory_fraction and max_num_batched_tokens
Drop page cache: sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'
Call torch.cuda.empty_cache() between samples in eval loops
Disable swap and run workloads under systemd-run -p MemoryMax
Upgrade to driver >= 580.159.03 which improves OOM handling

candidate_rules.trigger: MemAvailable < 16 GiB or /proc/pressure/memory some avg10 > threshold or swap in use on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: MemAvailable={memavail} of MemTotal={memtotal}; PSI memory some/full avg10={psi}; SwapUsed={swap}; heavy GPU processes: {procs}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: GPU and CPU share one pool; cudaMemGetInfo under-reports and free -g misleads, so pressure must be read from MemAvailable/PSI. With swap enabled the machine can go 'zombie' instead of failing cleanly.
next_steps: sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'
Stop concurrent model servers (Ollama + vLLM co-tenancy)
sudo swapoff -a and comment swap in /etc/fstab
Protect sshd with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 drop-in

candidate_rules.trigger: SwapTotal > 0 on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Swap enabled: {swap_devices} ({swaptotal}).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Community guidance for unified memory is to disable swap so OOM fails fast rather than thrashing; issue #97's head node was swapping before its hard reset.
next_steps: sudo swapoff -a; comment swap entries in /etc/fstab
Use cgroup MemoryMax jails for training jobs

candidate_rules.trigger: Under load GPU SM clock < 1400 MHz and power.draw < 20 W while pstate P0 (typical 611 MHz / 13 W / ~50 C)
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Load test: clocks.sm={clk} MHz, power.draw={pw} W, temp={t} C, pstate={ps}; healthy GB10 ~2200-2480 MHz / 80-93 W.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: USB-C PD controller wedge in the 240 W brick caps the SoC; pstate still reads P0 so naive checks pass while throughput collapses ~4x.
next_steps: Cold drain: shutdown, unplug PSU and all USB-C, hold power 30 s, wait 60 s, reconnect PSU only, boot
Use only the supplied power adapter (NVIDIA known issue)
After recovery: sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades && sudo fwupdmgr update; cold-drain again

candidate_rules.trigger: last -Fx shows boots without shutdown records and previous journal ends abruptly; /sys/fs/pstore empty
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {n} unexplained power losses in {days} days (last {ts}); no OOM/panic/Xid/thermal entries; pstore empty; crashkernel={ck}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: GB10 embedded controller can cut power faster than Linux logs; community fleet eliminated crashes with a clock cap while NVIDIA RMA'd units (fielddiag thermal error 082-000-1-020000600139).
next_steps: Trial: sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200 (persist via systemd unit); revert with nvidia-smi -rgc
Check firmware via fwupdmgr get-devices and update through DGX Dashboard
Improve airflow; verify PSU; open NVIDIA support case if persists

candidate_rules.trigger: nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK shows locked/applications clocks below default or gb10-clock-cap.service enabled
candidate_rules.evidence_template: GPU clocks locked to {min}-{max} MHz (default max ~2418 MHz); service gb10-clock-cap.service={state}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Explains ~5% lower throughput in benchmarks and indicates a prior stability workaround.
next_steps: Document as intentional or revert with sudo nvidia-smi -rgc

candidate_rules.trigger: GPU idle (util 0%) yet temperature > 55 C and power > 11 W for > 30 min after load
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Idle GPU at {t} C / {pw} W for {mins} min (baseline 38-40 C / 8-10 W); fan speed reported {fan}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Reported Sept 2026 on 580.173.02; only a reboot restored baseline; fan telemetry is [N/A] so thermal state must be inferred.
next_steps: Confirm no residual processes hold the GPU
Reboot if persistent; report on NVIDIA forum with nvidia-smi -q

candidate_rules.trigger: CX-7 interface (enp1s0f*np*, enP2p1s0f*np*) is Up with an IP but MTU is 1500
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {iface} ({rdma_dev}) MTU={mtu}; RoCE saturation needs 9000.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Issue #102 shows NCCL plateauing at ~3 GB/s with default MTU and reaching 23.7 GB/s (~190 Gbps) with MTU 9000 + NCCL_IB_HCA pinning.
next_steps: Set mtu: 9000 in /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml or nmcli 802-3-ethernet.mtu 9000 on every node
Validate with ping -c 2 -M do -s 8000 <peer>
Export NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0 (and NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3 if 'ibv_modify_qp failed 101')

candidate_rules.trigger: Two logical CX-7 interfaces of the same physical port (enp1s0f0np0 and enP2p1s0f0np0) carry IPs in the same /24
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {if1}={ip1} and {if2}={ip2} share subnet {subnet}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: NCCL errors 'Interfaces X and Y share the same subnet' and bandwidth halves; playbooks require distinct subnets (e.g. 192.168.100.x and 192.168.101.x).
next_steps: Assign separate subnets per logical interface on both nodes
When two QSFP cables are connected, give all four interfaces IPs

candidate_rules.trigger: CX-7 interface has an IP but no /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml (or NetworkManager profile) defines it
candidate_rules.evidence_template: {iface} has {ip} but no persistent netplan/nmcli config found.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: ip addr add configuration is lost on reboot, breaking clusters silently.
next_steps: Create /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml (chmod 600) and sudo netplan apply

candidate_rules.trigger: dmesg contains mlx5 'insufficient power' PCIe warnings on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: mlx5 PCIe 'insufficient power' warning at boot ({count}); known benign on DGX Spark.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Prevents a false CRIT from generic dmesg scanning.
next_steps: Ignore unless accompanied by actual throttling (see gb10.pd_power_throttle)

candidate_rules.trigger: Locally built NCCL (~/nccl/build) or nccl-tests lacks sm_121 (cuobjdump shows no sm_121/compute_121), or NCCL built from a dev branch rather than a release tag
candidate_rules.evidence_template: NCCL at {path} built with arch {archs}; playbook requires NVCC_GENCODE="-gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121" from tag v2.30.7-1 (v2.28.9-1 also validated).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Dev-branch builds plateaued at 3 GB/s; wrong arch fails at runtime.
next_steps: git clone -b v2.30.7-1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl.git && make -j src.build NVCC_GENCODE="-gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121"
Avoid 16G all_gather_perf test (~32 GB/node) with a desktop session active; use -b 512M -e 4G -f 2

candidate_rules.trigger: nvidia-device-plugin image tag < v0.17.4 on a GB10 node, or CrashLoopBackOff with 'error getting device memory: Not Supported'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Device plugin {image} on GB10 node {node}; pod status {status}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Older plugins crash on nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo; GPU Operator #1794 and #1482 confirm; MPS on GB10 also reported failing ('getpwuid() failed for 0'), leaving time-slicing as the sharing option.
next_steps: Upgrade to k8s-device-plugin >= v0.17.4 or a GPU Operator release bundling it
Prefer time-slicing over MPS on GB10

candidate_rules.trigger: vLLM command line contains --kv-cache-dtype fp8 and logs show 'fp8_gemm_sm100' / 'CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED_CUDA_DRIVER' / 'Engine core initialization failed.'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: vLLM {version} + FlashInfer {fi_version} failed engine init with '{error}' using --kv-cache-dtype fp8 on sm_121.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: FlashInfer routes FP8 GEMM to an SM100 cuDNN path on SM12x; the published Nemotron-3.5-Lightning recipe fails as written.
next_steps: Remove --kv-cache-dtype fp8
Track playbook issue #107 / FlashInfer fix

candidate_rules.trigger: vllm serve running with --gpu-memory-utilization >= 0.9 on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: vLLM launched with --gpu-memory-utilization {val} on 128 GB unified memory; vLLM's DGX Spark guidance suggests ~0.85 and treating it as a tuning knob.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: On UMA the fraction is of shared system RAM; 0.9 starves OS/page cache/other engines and precedes NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY resets.
next_steps: Lower to 0.75-0.85; reduce --max-model-len / --max-num-seqs
Use --linear-backend/--moe-backend CLI flags instead of deprecated VLLM_NVFP4_GEMM_BACKEND / VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4 env vars

candidate_rules.trigger: Running/pulled image nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:<=25.09-py3 (or other NGC tag from before sm_121 support) on GB10
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Image {image} predates GB10 support; torch.cuda.is_available() inside returns {avail}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: nvidia-smi works inside the container but PyTorch has no sm_121 kernels (unsloth #3553).
next_steps: Use nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.10-py3 or newer (playbooks use 25.11-py3)
Use nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05.post1-py3 / tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc13 per playbooks

candidate_rules.trigger: trtllm-serve logs contain 'attention sinks is only supported on SM90' or 'TRTLLMGenFusedMoE does not support SM120 and above'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: TensorRT-LLM {version} hit '{error}' on GB10 (SM121).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: GPT-OSS and MoE models need SM120-compatible backends; TRT-LLM Spark support is beta (single node only).
next_steps: Use TRT-LLM >= 1.2 (playbook: release:1.3.0rc13) and moe_config.backend TRITON or CUTLASS per model
export TRT_LLM_DISABLE_LOAD_WEIGHTS_IN_PARALLEL=1 on weight-loading OOM

candidate_rules.trigger: nvcc missing from PATH, nvcc major version != driver-reported CUDA major (13), or /usr/local/cuda not pointing at cuda-13.x
candidate_rules.evidence_template: nvcc={nvcc_version} at {path}; nvidia-smi CUDA Version {drv_cuda}; /usr/local/cuda -> {link}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: llama.cpp/NCCL builds fail ('CUDA not found') or compile for wrong toolkit; Triton needs the CUDA 13 ptxas.
next_steps: export PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64
Install toolkit via NVIDIA sbsa runfile with Driver unchecked if apt metapackages are absent

candidate_rules.trigger: bitsandbytes installed on GB10 and BNB_CUDA_VERSION unset while system CUDA is 13.1+
candidate_rules.evidence_template: bitsandbytes {version}; BNB_CUDA_VERSION={val}; system CUDA {cuda}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: NVIDIA's performance guide forces BNB_CUDA_VERSION=130 because 'CUDA 13.1 not yet supported' by bitsandbytes binaries.
next_steps: export BNB_CUDA_VERSION=130

candidate_rules.trigger: Two or more of ollama (11434), vllm (8000), sglang (30000), llama-server, trtllm-serve (8355) are running with models loaded
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Concurrent engines: {engines}; combined RSS {rss}; MemAvailable {memavail}.
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: Ollama + vLLM co-tenancy on the 128 GB pool caused OOMs that motivated the memory dashboard; there is no VRAM partition to protect either process.
next_steps: Unload idle models (ollama stop / curl /api/ps) or stop one server
Budget with 'CAN I LOAD NEXT?' style headroom = MemAvailable - model size - KV cache

candidate_rules.trigger: nsys invoked with --cuda-um-*-page-faults on GB10 or log shows 'Unified Memory trace is not supported'
candidate_rules.evidence_template: Nsight Systems {version}: UVM tracing unsupported on GB10 (driver {driver}).
candidate_rules.why_it_matters: NVIDIA confirms UVM profiling is not yet supported on Spark; avoid misdiagnosing as a driver fault.
next_steps: Drop UM tracing flags; use standard CUDA trace

commands_and_flags.command: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,pstate,clocks.sm,power.draw,temperature.gpu,fan.speed,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
commands_and_flags.notes: On GB10 name='NVIDIA GB10'; memory.* and fan.speed return N/A / Not Supported (expected). Driver seen in the wild: 580.95.05 (Oct 2025), 580.126.09, 580.142 (Mar 2026), 580.159.03 (Jun 2026, OTA2607), 580.173.02 (Aug 2026); 595.58.03 in one k8s report.

commands_and_flags.notes: MemAvailable is 'correct on GB10 UMA'; cudaMemGetInfo and free -g under-report allocatable memory.

commands_and_flags.notes: Perf guide variant: -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="121a" -DGGML_CUDA_CUB_3DOT2=on. Fallback "121" on wrong-arch errors.

commands_and_flags.command: git clone -b v2.30.7-1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl.git ~/nccl && cd ~/nccl && make -j src.build NVCC_GENCODE="-gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121"; git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests.git ~/nccl-tests && cd ~/nccl-tests && make MPI=1; export UCX_NET_DEVICES=enP7s7 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enP7s7 OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=enP7s7; mpirun -np 2 -H <ip1>:1,<ip2>:1 --mca plm_rsh_agent "ssh -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no" -x LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH $HOME/nccl-tests/build/all_gather_perf -b 512M -e 4G -f 2

For full bandwidth add NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0 and MTU 9000; ring topology: NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1 NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none; single-cable dual: NCCL_IB_MERGE_NICS=0 NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3. commands_and_flags.notes: ~5% throughput cost; persists only while driver loaded (nvidia-persistenced default). systemd unit gb10-clock-cap.service in the repo.
